content:
I fully admit my DIY iPhone camera hack looks pretty ridiculous—but it genuinely makes using my iPhone to take photos more practical and more enjoyable.

It started as a fix for one specific video shoot, but I ended up using it way more than I expected…

In the world of compact cameras, whether to have a viewfinder has always been a major divide. Once upon a time, photography enthusiasts would also argue endlessly about whether an electronic viewfinder (EVF) or an optical viewfinder was better, but EVFs are now so good that hardly anyone cares anymore.

But whether optical or electronic, a viewfinder offers very real advantages over composing on the rear screen—especially when shooting in harsh sunlight. Even with screen brightness cranked all the way up, it can be very hard to see what you are shooting when the sun is strong, and screen reflections are also a problem.

Living in London, this has never really been a huge issue for me, but after this summer's record-breaking heatwave, honestly it feels like the last time I saw a cloud or rain was about thirty years ago.

But for me it means more than that. I think there is a psychological, visual difference—between only seeing what falls within the frame of your photo, and seeing the surroundings around you as you take it. Sometimes it is exactly that feeling that makes me reach for a dedicated camera rather than my iPhone.

When I chose a video camera a few years ago, the Blackmagic Pocket Cinema Camera 4K was clearly the runaway favourite, but the lack of a viewfinder did give me pause. In the end I decided it wasn't a big deal for me, because I mainly shoot indoors, and when I need to use it outside, attaching a large monitor with a sun hood solves most of the problem.

But sometimes I want to use it in a more portable form than a full-frame rig with a monitor, so I found a simple accessory that does the job outdoors. It's a two-in-one sun hood and magnifying lens that magnetically attaches to the camera's rear screen, effectively giving you an optical viewfinder.

I had an upcoming shoot where I needed to record video on both the BMPCC 4K and my iPhone 16 Pro Max. I did a quick test on location and found the viewfinder accessory really useful. Since the screens on the BMPCC 4K and the iPhone are pretty close in size, I wondered if it would work on the iPhone.

Of course the iPhone has no magnets, but the iPhone is light enough that holding it up against the magnifier is no problem at all. To my surprise, it worked brilliantly—especially because I use the Camera Control button as a shutter.

Since then, I've found myself reaching for it all the time when shooting photos, enjoying the convenience of being able to see the screen more easily in harsh sunlight, and that feeling of immersion. My iPhone became my main camera a long time ago, and with this DIY mod, I feel like a phone is all I need in even more situations.

Genius or ridiculous? Let me know your thoughts in the comments. If you think it's the former, unfortunately the product I bought seems to have been discontinued, and I haven't yet seen anything similar designed for screens larger than three inches. If you find one, drop a link in the comments.
